title: O God, Our Help in Ages Past (closed SATB: crossings and unisons)

expected.notes: Closed score without any part labels: the converter must infer S/A from stem direction on the treble staff (stem up = Soprano, stem down = Alto) and T/B on the bass staff, even where the voices cross (m.3 beat 3 and m.10 the alto is ABOVE the soprano; m.12 the tenor is BELOW the bass). Unisons: shared note heads with two stems (mm.4, 10, 14, and T+B in m.7) belong to BOTH parts; in m.6 beat 3 the alto unison is drawn with one head and only the soprano's up-stem (the alto still sings a' there - the down-stem was omitted); in m.13 the soprano half note and the alto quarter on the same pitch are two separate heads. Alto rests on m.7 beat 3. Both verses are printed under the treble staff and are aligned to the soprano; truth carries them on the Soprano part only (the other parts sing the same words but the score does not print them for them). Pickup bar is measure 0.

title: Nun danket alle Gott (closed SATB, German, lyrics under both staves, lyrics switch voice)

expected.notes: Closed score with German labels "Sopran/Alt" and "Tenor/Bass" (abbreviated "S./A.", "T./B." on later systems). Split each staff by stem direction into four parts. There is one lyric line under EACH staff: the upper line belongs to the Sopran, except mm.9-10 where the Sopran has whole-bar rests and the same line carries the Alt echo "an uns und allen Enden"; the lower line belongs to the Bass, except mm.9-10 where the Bass rests and the line belongs to the Tenor. In m.3 the Bass sings a dotted rhythm, so its syllable "Her-" sits half a beat after the Sopran's. A correct conversion attaches each syllable to the voice whose note it is printed under (truth: Sopran mm.1-8,11-12; Alt mm.9-10; Bass mm.1-8,11-12; Tenor mm.9-10).

title: All Things Bright and Beautiful (SAB: 3 parts on 2 staves, cross-staff alto)

expected.notes: SAB closed score: Soprano (stems up) and Alto (stems down) share the treble staff; the Baritone is alone on the bass staff (its stems point both ways and must NOT be split into two parts). In m.4 the alto line moves down onto the bass staff (c#' then a, stems up, above the baritone's down-stem notes) while the soprano is alone on the treble staff: those two alto notes belong to the Alto part, not to the Baritone and not to a new part. Expected output: exactly 3 parts. Two verses under the treble staff, aligned to the Soprano (truth: Soprano only).

title: Ave verum corpus (open score; divisi appears mid-piece)

expected.notes: Open score, one staff per part, every staff labelled (full names on page 1, then S./A./T./B.). MUST NOT create extra parts for the divisi passages: in mm.7-8 the Tenor staff splits into two voices ("div.", stems up/down, back to "unis." in m.9) - both voices belong to the Tenor part (truth: Tenor voice 1 and voice 2); in m.18 and mm.20-21 the Soprano sings two-note chords on one stem and in mm.20-21 the Bass sings octave chords: these stay chords inside Soprano/Bass. Exactly 4 parts. The tenor clef is a treble clef with a small 8 below (sounds an octave lower than written): truth pitches are sounding pitches (e.g. m.16 tenor B3 natural). Lyrics are printed under every staff and belong to each part (the second tenor voice in mm.7-8 has none).

title: Integer vitae (TTBB closed score, octave treble clef, a 2 / unis.)

title: Love Came Down at Christmas (SSAA on two treble staves + piano)

expected.notes: Two choir staves, BOTH in treble clef (Soprano I/II, Alto I/II) - do not mistake the alto staff for a second soprano part or for a piano right hand. Split each choir staff by stem direction into two parts (4 choir parts). The piano grand staff (brace, "Piano") is ONE part with two staves: its right hand has two voices (melody stems up, two-note chords stems down) and the left hand plays bass + chords - none of this may be split into separate parts and the chords stay chords. Choir is tacet in mm.1-2 (one merged whole-bar rest per choir staff stands for both parts). Two verses under the upper choir staff, aligned to Soprano I.

title: Hark! the Herald Angels Sing (closed SATB, S A / T B labels, ties vs re-attacks, bass solo, chords on one stem)

expected.notes: Closed score labelled only "S A" and "T B". mm.1-2: soprano and alto sing the same notes (every head carries an up- and a down-stem) - both parts get the full phrase. m.4-5: the soprano g' is TIED over the barline while the alto RE-ATTACKS g' on m.5 beat 1 (same head position): truth has a tie in Soprano and a new note in Alto; the same happens in mm.7-8 on the bass staff (tenor a tied, bass re-attacks a). mm.5-6: upper voices and tenor rest while the bass sings a solo whose words ("Peace on earth, and mercy mild") are printed under the bass staff and belong to the Bass. m.7: alto enters after a quarter rest. Amen (mm.9-10): the soprano sings two-note chords on its up-stem and the bass octaves on its down-stem - these must stay chords inside Soprano/Bass (must_not_split refers to these chords), the alto and tenor single notes are separate parts. Exactly 4 parts.
